The verification failure is fixed. Summary:

## What was wrong

`desktop/node_modules` did not exist in this worktree, so `npx --prefix desktop tsc` fetched the decoy `tsc` package from the registry and exited 1. Nothing in the slice was ever compiled.

## What I changed

**`tasks/ui-split.md`** — the only tracked file modified:
- Added `setup: npm ci --prefix desktop` so the engine creates `node_modules` before implement rather than relying on it being there (the engine runs `setup:` only when the front matter declares one).
- Changed `test_commands` from `npx --prefix desktop tsc --noEmit -p desktop` to `npm --prefix desktop run typecheck`. The old command was vacuous even when it worked: `desktop/tsconfig.json` is a solution file with `"files": []`, so `-p desktop` checked zero files and would have passed no matter what the slice wrote. `typecheck` runs the node + web projects, which actually compile `src/`.

I verified these grant a future stage what it needs: `command_tool_rules` derives `Bash(npm --prefix:*)` and `Bash(npm ci:*)` from the two new lines (`aidev/pipeline.py:719`).

## Two things the report did not anticipate

**The task file was cp949-encoded, not UTF-8.** It is the only file in `tasks/` that doesn't match a UTF-8 Korean grep. Something re-encoded it with `errors="replace"` — most likely the `Set-Content` in commit `4f6e848` ("분량 경고 - 180 상향") — and cp949 has no U+2014, so all four em dashes had already been destroyed to `?`. `aidev/pipeline.py:5308` reads task files with strict UTF-8, so `aidev run tasks/ui-split.md` would have crashed. Editing it with Edit/Write would have turned the Korean body into U+FFFD, so I did a byte-level repair instead: decode cp949 → restore the em dashes → write UTF-8. The body now matches the pipeline's own pristine `requirement.md` copy.
